steps.what: Review shipment requirements and available carrier rates and capacity
Negotiate transport terms with shipping or freight companies
Enter the agreed carrier, rate and service conditions in the shipment record
Prepare and check the carrier booking message from the recorded arrangement
Send the checked transport booking to the selected carrier

tasks.design: Configure a carrier-offer view, an arrangement form and a booking-message template in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {EMAIL}. The agent negotiates, records the actual agreement, checks the populated message and separately sends the final booking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rate comparison, recording the agreement and rebuilding a booking message require repeated navigation and typing.
tasks.enabler_now: A native shipment record can reuse existing addresses and cargo details while the agent supplies negotiated terms.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain capacity, surcharges and exceptions require negotiation rather than a mechanical lowest-price choice.
tasks.human_edge: Reaching a credible agreement and recognising a service promise the carrier cannot meet.
tasks.altitude: Less booking assembly, with unchanged negotiating authority.

reach.task: Check whether a carrier service meets the shipment's constraints
reach.learn: Service inclusions, surcharges and capacity limitations

evidence.claim: Boltrics provides transport and forwarding software; this supports the system category, not the specific local booking saving.
Native carrier views, editable booking templates and their time estimates are model knowledge designs.

assumptions: Boundary includes the negotiation, real agreement record, booking-message preparation and send. Choosing the shipment mode and preparing transport documents are in task 8192; no duplicate savings are assigned to those actions.

The customer order supplies shipment ID, pickup and delivery locations, cargo, weight, ready time and deadline. s1 counts checking these for carrier suitability, not recreating the order. The carrier supplies rate, currency, inclusions, availability and offer expiry during existing offers and s2; absent data require manual clarification, fully retained in s2.

The agent produces carrier ID, agreed price, service, collection window and conditions in s3. Its retained 13 hours include field capture and confirmation; s4's retained 10 hours include checking addresses, cargo and negotiated exceptions in the final booking. No structured agreement is assumed to appear from the call automatically.

Test native views and templates first. Ordinary arrangement saves have no gate or saving; s3's benefit is reuse of already verified shipment fields. The real external send remains fully retained and separately gated.
unknowns: Current native booking templates and rate-view coverage
Actual amount of repeated field entry after negotiations
research_questions: Does template reuse reduce booking preparation without losing negotiated exceptions?

tasks.short: Select shipment method and prepare documents

steps.what: Verify the shipment particulars required for transport documents
Determine the method of shipment from cargo and service requirements
Prepare bills of lading from the verified shipment record
Prepare the shipment invoice from verified billing data
Prepare other shipment-specific shipping documents required for this movement
Check the completed shipping documents for consistency and missing particulars

tasks.design: Configure native bill-of-lading and invoice drafts in {OPS_SYSTEM} using one verified shipment record. The agent selects the shipment method, adapts additional forms in {DOCS} and checks the prepared package; signing, issuing, ledger posting and sending are separate downstream actions with no saving claimed here.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same shipment particulars are repeatedly copied into different document layouts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native transport document and invoice templates can reuse verified fields without a narrative model.
tasks.still_hard: Missing cargo particulars, unusual movements and document requirements that differ by route or mode.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when the standard documents do not represent the actual shipment.
tasks.altitude: More exception checking and less repeated document typing, with unchanged shipment-method decisions.

reach.task: Identify which transport documents a particular movement requires

evidence.claim: Qargo and TransFollow support creation of consignment documents within the transport system.
The Mark Huisman Logistics vendor case reports a large reduction in invoicing work; its weekly workflow is context and not this task's estimated saving.
Draft-only template field reuse and all task-specific time estimates are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is selecting the transport method and preparing the actual bills, invoice and additional documents. No legal signature, issue, invoice posting or send is implied by creating a draft. Carrier negotiation and booking are separately counted in task 8188.

The agent verifies and, where needed, enters shipment ID, shipper, consignee, pickup and delivery address, package count, cargo description, gross weight and unit, references, agreed charge, currency, tax treatment and billing party in s1. The customer supplies cargo and address particulars; commercial records supply charges. Its retained 17 hours count capture and missing-data resolution, not free extraction.

The agent produces the method decision in s2 and confirms required document type and template version. s3-s4 use only those fields; missing mandatory values block formatting and return to s1 manual entry. Specialist content in additional documents remains human in s5. s6 counts all final consistency checking.

Test native transport-system templates before custom code. Ordinary author saves have no gate or saving, and existing runtime is not baseline human effort. Machine shares represent today's manual draft formatting only.
unknowns: Current share of bills and invoices already populated natively
Compatibility of native templates with route-specific requirements
research_questions: Can a sample of actual movements produce correct draft documents without additional data capture or re-keying?

incremental.description: Maintain document mappings and test layout and tax-field changes

steps.what: Retrieve delivery progress from carrier tracking sources
Assess whether the observed progress meets the delivery commitment
Clarify missing or contradictory delivery information with the carrier
Update the shipment's delivery progress record with the checked facts

tasks.design: Use existing carrier-status views and a run-linked update form in {OPS_SYSTEM}, retaining {PARTNER_PORTAL} lookup when native coverage is absent. The agent interprets progress, makes the actual clarification call and separately records the checked update; no automatic alert or customer send is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tracking references and carrier updates must be found and then copied into the shipment record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native status views can reduce portal navigation and reuse verified event references in an editable update form.
tasks.still_hard: A stale carrier scan or estimated arrival does not prove delivery or explain a delay.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a progress claim requires a carrier conversation rather than another screen refresh.
tasks.altitude: Less lookup and transcription while exception chasing remains with the agent.

reach.task: Clarify a missing milestone affecting the transport chain
reach.learn: Carrier event meanings and milestone provenance

evidence.claim: Portbase offers import-status visibility and port message services; this supports a limited status-source capability, not universal carrier tracking.
Native status-view and editable event-reference reuse are model knowledge designs with locally unmeasured time savings.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual lookup, judgement, carrier clarification and the working shipment progress record. Customer notifications and rerouting are not implied or credited; the record is the operational tracking record, not an added report.

Carriers produce tracking reference, event code and text, event time and time zone, location, reported ETA and update timestamp in their existing systems. s1 counts reference matching and provenance reading; missing events remain missing. s3 counts all manual clarification rather than assuming a free discrepancy flag.

The agent produces the assessed progress in s2 and records checked event references, current status, uncertainty and follow-up need in s4. Its retained 12 hours include capture and verification. Unmapped status text or uncertain identity requires manual lookup and entry, not inferred delivery.

Test native views and forms before new integrations. Existing carrier runtime earns no saving; s1's reduction is actual lookup navigation and s4's reduction is repeated field transcription. Same-system save time stays negligible and ungated.
unknowns: Carrier coverage and freshness of native tracking views
Current share of status entries already linked to events
research_questions: Does native status reuse reduce total lookup and entry effort without obscuring stale or estimated information?

tasks.short: Advise clients on transport and payment

steps.what: Clarify the client's cargo, timing and payment requirements
Look up transport services and applicable payment terms
Choose a suitable transport recommendation and explain payment trade-offs
Write the transport and payment advice for the client
Send the final advice message to the client
Answer the client's follow-up questions about the recommendation

tasks.design: Configure a current service-and-payment view in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}, plus editable advice snippets in {EMAIL}. The agent chooses the recommendation, checks the client-specific written advice and separately sends it, retaining all clarification and follow-up conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current service terms and standard payment explanations are scattered across working documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document search and checked message snippets can remove lookup navigation and repeated standard wording.
tasks.still_hard: Cargo suitability and a client's understanding of risk and payment obligations.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a recommendation in the client's circumstances without promising unavailable service or credit.
tasks.altitude: Less lookup and routine wording, with unchanged advice responsibility.

reach.task: Explain service and payment consequences for a proposed shipment
reach.learn: Service limitations and escalation for nonstandard credit terms

evidence.claim: Native service lookup and editable advice snippets are model knowledge designs; the digest provides no measured saving for client advice.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual written advice and send as well as conversation. It assumes the common case with an advice email; purely spoken enquiries have no invented trailing record and no writing benefit. Booking, document preparation and progress tracking remain in their separate tasks.

The client supplies cargo, route, timing and payment needs in s1; their clarification time is fully retained. Existing service owners supply service availability, restrictions, payment methods, due dates and versioned terms in maintained documents. s2 counts source and applicability checking; missing terms require manual clarification.

The agent produces the recommendation in s3 and captures the specific recommendation, conditions, client address and source terms in s4. Its retained 13 hours include writing nonstandard content and checking the final message. No structured customer preference is assumed without this capture.

Test native views and message snippets before custom code. No model or automated send is needed. Ordinary draft saves have no gate or saving; gates cover live external advice and the final message send.
unknowns: Share of enquiries with a real written recommendation
Availability and maintenance of current service and payment terms
research_questions: Do snippets reduce writing time while keeping nonstandard cargo and payment caveats explicit?
